upload.choose: Pick a plain-text or Markdown file from your computer. Turbine reads it here in the browser and keeps a copy on the server so a job can keep running when this tab is closed.
upload.drop: You can also drag a .md or .txt file from your desktop and drop it anywhere in this box.
upload.remove: Forget this document in Turbine. The original file on your computer is untouched.

stats.characters: Every letter, space and punctuation mark, counted once. Character positions are what selections are measured in.
stats.words: Whitespace-separated words. A printed page holds about 275.
stats.tokens: Tokens are the pieces a language model actually reads, roughly three quarters of an English word each. This is what fills the model's context and what you pay for. Estimated from the text; exact once the tokenizer has loaded.
stats.pages: Estimated printed pages at 275 words per page.
stats.paragraphs: Blocks separated by a blank line. The viewer renders them in batches, and windows prefer to end at a paragraph boundary.

selection.tokens: How much of the model's attention the highlighted text takes. Counted exactly with the built-in tokenizer once it has loaded (before that it is an estimate), and replaced by the model's own count after a preview.
selection.chars: Character positions of the highlighted span in the file: where it starts, where it ends, how long it is. Useful for repeating a selection; not what the model measures.
selection.clear: Drop the highlight. Preview will go back to using the first planned window.

viewer.jump: Jump to a place in the document by percentage, 0 to 100.
viewer.load_more: Show the next batch of paragraphs. Long books load in chunks so scrolling stays smooth.
viewer.text: Select any span, even a single line, to use it as the preview focus. The highlight is remembered on the Prompt tab.

instructions.system: Your standing orders, sent with every window as the system message: what the model should do to each piece of text and what it must leave alone.
instructions.reset: Restore Turbine's default prompts: careful Markdown cleanup that preserves the author's words.

template.user: How each window is packaged for the model. {{focus}} is the slice to transform; the context blocks are read-only neighbours; anything inside {{#name}}…{{/name}} appears only when that variable has content.
template.chips: Click to insert this variable at the cursor.

window.focus_tokens: How big each slice to transform is, in tokens. Bigger slices mean fewer windows and more coherent output, but each call takes longer and a failure loses more.
window.context_before: Read-only text shown to the model just before the slice, so it knows what it is continuing from. Never transformed, never repeated in the output.
window.context_after: Read-only text shown just after the slice, so the model knows what comes next. Never transformed, never repeated in the output.
window.snap: Where a slice is allowed to end: at a paragraph break (cleanest), at the end of a sentence, or simply at the nearest space.
window.only_selection: Run the job on the highlighted selection only, instead of the whole document.

run.mode: map: windows run side by side and are stitched together by position. fold: windows run one after another and each sees the tail of the previous output. Use fold when continuity matters, such as numbering or a running tone.
run.concurrency: How many windows run at the same time in map mode. A local machine usually handles one or two; hosted APIs handle more.
run.carry_kind: In fold mode, what each window gets from the one before it: the tail of the previous output, or nothing.
run.carry_chars: How many characters of the previous output to carry forward.
run.max_tokens: The most the model may write for one window. Auto keeps it at about 1.5× the largest slice plus a margin, so nothing is cut off. A manual value smaller than a slice will truncate that window's output.
run.max_tokens_auto: Let Turbine size the output limit from the largest slice in the plan and the model's context. Untick to set it by hand.
run.validator: A check on every window's output before it is accepted. conserve: the words must survive and only formatting may change. length ratio: the output must stay within a size band of the input.
run.threshold: Minimum similarity for conserve, from 0 to 1. Turbine strips Markdown from the output, normalises case, quotes and punctuation, then compares the two word sequences with a longest-common-subsequence match. 1.0 means every word survived in order; 0.95 tolerates about one word in twenty added, dropped or changed. Raise it for pure formatting, lower it for translation or rewriting.
run.min_ratio: Smallest acceptable output length as a fraction of the input length. 0.5 means the output may shrink to half.
run.max_ratio: Largest acceptable output length as a multiple of the input length. 2 means the output may double.
run.attempts: How many tries a window gets. Each retry lowers the temperature. After the last try the best attempt is kept and the window is flagged for review.

plan.windows: How many slices the document (or the selection) splits into with the current settings.
plan.avg_prompt: Average size of what the model reads per window: instructions, template, context and focus.
plan.max_prompt: The biggest single prompt in the plan. It must fit inside the model's context together with the output limit.
plan.ctx: The model's context length from your connection settings. Prompt plus output must fit inside it.
plan.total_tokens: Everything the model will read and write across the whole job, added up. Roughly what the job costs.
plan.eta: Wall-clock estimate. Until you run a preview it assumes 20 seconds per window; afterwards it uses the speed the preview measured.
plan.truncate: The output limit is smaller than the largest slice, so that window's output may be cut off mid-text.
plan.start: Create the job and start it. It runs on the server (or in this tab for a local backend under a public deployment) and you can watch it on the Output tab.

focus.header: The text Preview will transform. Select any span in the viewer; with no selection the first planned window is used.
focus.tokens: Size of the focus in tokens. Exact with the built-in tokenizer; the model's own count is shown after a preview.
focus.clear: Drop the selection and go back to previewing the first window.

preview.run: Send just this focus to the model with the real instructions and context, and stream the result here. Nothing is saved.
preview.messages: The exact messages the model receives after the template is filled in.
preview.output: The model's answer, streaming in. The pane follows the newest text while you are at the bottom; scroll up to read, scroll back down to follow again.
preview.tokens: Tokens generated so far, refreshed about once a second. When the model finishes, its exact count replaces the running figure.

model.panel: Knobs the backend reports for the connected model, discovered from its own endpoints (Ollama's show, OpenRouter's model list, vLLM and llama.cpp metadata, Anthropic's model info). Anything you leave blank is not sent, so the backend's defaults apply.
model.refresh: Ask the backend again. Do this after pulling a new model or changing the connection.
model.reset: Back to Turbine's defaults: reasoning off, temperature from config, every other knob cleared so the backend decides.
model.reasoning: Whether the model thinks before answering. Off is Turbine's default for every backend: formatting jobs want the transformation, not the deliberation, and thinking tokens cost time and money. Where a model always reasons, off is not offered and the lowest effort is used instead.
model.knob_clear: Clear this knob so it is not sent and the backend's own default applies.

status.state: Where the job is: running, paused, completed, cancelled, halted on an error, or waiting for you to unlock an expired key.
status.progress: Windows finished out of the total, with any flagged (failed validation) or failed (no usable output) counts.
status.eta: Time so far and the remaining-time estimate based on the windows completed in this run.
status.tokens: Tokens the model has read and written so far, as reported by the backend.
status.where: Which connection and model are doing the work, and whether the calls come from the server or this tab.
status.socket: State of the live event stream from the server. It reconnects on its own.

controls.pause: Let the windows already in flight finish, then stop starting new ones.
controls.resume: Continue from the checkpoint. Finished windows are not redone.
controls.cancel: Stop the job for good. Everything finished so far stays saved and can still be downloaded.
controls.save: Download the output as it exists right now, named after the source with __transformed added. Windows still pending are marked in the file.
controls.copy: Copy the current output to the clipboard.
controls.clear: Forget this job in this browser and empty the Output view. Disabled while the job is running or paused. The server keeps the job's checkpoint file, but nothing here will show it again.

windows.chips: One square per window in document order. Grey is pending, blue is running, green is done, amber failed validation, red produced nothing usable. Click one to run it again.

output.text: All finished windows stitched together in order. Failed windows pass their original text through behind a marker so nothing is silently lost.
output.live: Windows currently being generated, streaming in. Follows the newest text while you are at the bottom.

clear.save: Download the assembled output right now, exactly as shown, before clearing.
clear.slide: Drag the red knob all the way to the right to clear. Letting go early cancels. Keyboard: focus the knob and press End.
clear.keep: Close this warning and keep the output.

mode.local: Use a model running on your own machine or network: Ollama, vLLM or llama.cpp. No API key and no passphrase.
mode.remote: Use a hosted API such as OpenRouter, OpenAI or Anthropic. You will need an API key, protected here by a passphrase.

local.backend: Which local server you are running. Ollama speaks its own API; vLLM and llama.cpp speak the OpenAI-style API.
local.scheme: http for a plain local server; https if you put it behind TLS.
local.host: Where the server is: localhost for this machine, or a name or address on your network.
local.port: The port the server listens on. Ollama defaults to 11434, vLLM to 8000, llama.cpp to 8080.
local.path: Extra path after the port, usually /v1 for vLLM and llama.cpp and empty for Ollama.

connect.model: The model id exactly as the backend knows it. Use List models to see what is available.
connect.list_models: Ask the backend which models it has and pick one.
connect.ctx_len: How many tokens the model can hold at once, prompt and answer together. Turbine plans windows to stay inside it.

remote.base_url: The API's base address. Filled in for known providers; edit it for a custom OpenAI-compatible server.
remote.api_key: Your key for the provider. It is encrypted in this browser under your passphrase and held by the server only in memory, until the session timer runs out.
remote.passphrase: A short phrase only you know. It unlocks the encrypted key on later visits. It is never sent anywhere.

connect.test: Check that the backend answers and that the model exists, without starting anything.
connect.connect: Save this connection in this browser and start using it.
connect.unlock: Decrypt the saved key with your passphrase and reconnect.
connect.forget: Erase the connection and the encrypted key from this browser.
connect.different: Set up another connection instead of the saved one.
